column11: Bereshit Rabbah 65:1: ‘“Esau was forty years old, and he took as a wife Yehudit, daughter of Be'eri the Hitite, and Basmat, daughter of Elon the Hitite” (Genesis 26:34). “Esau was forty years old” – that is what is written: “The swine from the forest gnaws at it” (Psalms 80:14). Rabbi Pinḥas in the name of Rabbi Simon: Of all the prophets, only two of them publicized it – Moses and Asaf. Moses said: “The pig because it has a split hoof” (Deuteronomy 14:8). Asaf said: “The swine from the forest gnaws at it.” Why does he analogize it to a pig? This is why the Midrash says, “we think on the name of Avraham Avinu,” because “name” signifies will (desire). In a practical sense we find that some people are called on the name of their actions and artistry, since all their will and desire is included in the action that they are doing.

column11: Berakhot 59a: ‘The Gemara asks: And return it, why did the Holy One, Blessed be He, not restore the original two stars to Pleiades? The Gemara answers: A pit cannot be filled by its own earth; when a pit is excavated, the earth that was excavated from it is insufficient to refill it. Alternatively, one could say that a prosecutor cannot become an advocate; since these stars caused the flood it is not appropriate that they facilitate the end of the flood.’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 17, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Berakhot 59a) to illuminate his exposition here (“thinking that having attended the feast they were the sinners, and "an accuser cannot become a defender" (Berachos 59a); yet in truth they effected the primary miracle through their heartfelt...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.

column15: The Holy Yehudi of Pshiske explains this same verse by saying that God’s love for Israel is in the way of a segula, a hidden beloved treasure, as His reasons for this are hidden. also refers to a ritual or action that brings God’s goodness, yet with no obvious connection to the good effected, like how smelling the wick of the havdalla candle after the havdalla ceremony is believed to save one from anger, or a woman biting off the end of the etrog (citron) with the stem (pitom) after Succot is a segula for her to become pregnant.

column11: Megillah 12b: ‘“Carshena”; the ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, did the gentiles ever offer before You lambs [karim] of the first year [shana], as the Jewish people have offered before You? “Shethar”; have they ever offered before You two turtledoves [shetei torim]? “Admatha”; have they ever built before You an altar of earth [adama]? “Tarshish”; have they ever ministered before You in the priestly vestments, as it is written that on the fourth of the four rows of precious stones contained on the breastplate were: “A beryl [tarshish], an onyx, and a jasper” (Exodus 28:20).…’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 17, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Megillah 12b) to illuminate his exposition here (“Until Heaven placed it into the heart of Memuchan—who is Haman himself, as the Sages stated (Megillah 12b); that he himself should dig his own pit, preparing the cure for Israel's blow and...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.
column13: (a) It is related that the townspeople initially opposed the construction of the mausoleum, arguing that all the towering luminaries laid to rest in both the old and new cemeteries were buried without an ohel, and customs should not be changed for an individual. Rabbi Avraham Eiger convened a rabbinic court to deliberate the matter; relying on the talmudic ruling in Megillah 28b that eminent teachers who instruct others are not bound by ordinary limitations, they authorized the construction. This ohel was the first built in the historic city of Lublin.

column11: Megillah 12b: ‘The verse states: “And Memucan said” (Esther 1:16). A Sage taught in a baraita: Memucan is Haman. And why is Haman referred to as Memucan? Because he was prepared [mukhan] to bring calamity upon the Jewish people. Rav Kahana said: From here we see that the common man jumps to the front and speaks first, for Memucan was mentioned last of the king’s seven advisors, and nevertheless he expressed his opinion first.’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 17, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Megillah 12b) to illuminate his exposition here (“this explaining why he jumped forward to speak first (Megillah 12b), driven by intellectual arrogance; while "who is wise? column15: When a man gives birth to a Tsaddik, then the father has a connection to him, for the level of Tsidkut—righteousness—that is active in the son exists in a hidden way with the father. Yet when a sage is born to him, meaning wise in words of Torah, then he is a completely new birth, and the son has no connection to the father, for he is a new entity.
